title: Dance challenges Freeman's view of critics
summary: Dance calls his claim about critics too sweeping and describes growing to hear Charlie Parker; Freeman says the critic idolized only Lester.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, Bud, let me, since we are talking honestly and everything, let me take issue with you in a way. And that's simply this: Isn't that too sweeping a generalization?
No, no, I am just talking about the misinformed people who have written about jazz and made money. You know what I am talking about, because you and I have been friends for some 30 years.

Well, I have a tin ear in lots of places which I recognize. When I find myself not appreciating something in a certain area and I know where that is appreciated, I know that I have a tin ear in that respect.

But, excuse me, dear, I am only speaking of one incident. I am speaking, how was it possible for this critic to have loved my playing because Lester Young wanted to hear it. That's not possible. The critic was just being polite.

No Well, surely not, perhaps he actually -- I will tell you something, though, when I listened -- take sometime ago, listening to Charlie Parker who, after all, I preceded that generation, so Charlie Parker was not a musician who, his style, when he altered it, was not -- to me it was somewhat esoteric and it didn't register naturally and immediately with me.

And it was something that grew slowly on me, but when Dizzy would sing to me, what he was doing and what Charlie Parker was doing, I heard it then, where I didn't hear it instantly when Charlie Parker was doing it.

You have got to understand something. You have lived this music, you see. I am just talking about a man who idolized one person. He didn't idolize Duke Ellington and Louis. He idolized Lester, that was all there was to it, and everything he ever wrote, if he wrote
it was about Lester Young, a short story^A everything he wrote was about Lester Young.
Well, that is a bit off.
